What We Do

What SGA does

The Student Government Association is the official governing body of the student population. We represent students in the decisions of the College and oversee the allocation of the student activity fee.

Advocacy

We bring student concerns before the faculty and administration, from dining and housing to academic policy and campus safety.

Funding

Through the student activity fee, SGA charters student organizations and helps fund their events, projects, and programming.

Community

We support campus traditions such as Homecoming and Wise Winter Wonderland, and we hold meetings that are open to every student.

Cavs Help Cavs
Who We Are

Who we are

The Student Government Association is composed of students elected by their peers. The Senate meets throughout the fall and spring semesters, and every session is open to the student body.

  • An executive board and a Senate with seats for each class
  • Weekly meetings that are open to everyone
  • A direct line to the college's administration
  • A say in how the student activity budget is spent

Home / About

About the SGA

The Student Government Association is elected by students and accountable to students. This page outlines how it is organized and what it does.

Our Mission

What we're here for

The Student Government Association represents the students of the University of Virginia's College at Wise in all matters affecting student life and the College. Every degree-seeking student is a member.

We serve as the link between the student body and the College's administration, faculty, and staff. We carry student concerns forward, support organizations and activities, and work to improve the campus community. Our motto captures it: Cavs Help Cavs.

Of the students,
by the students,
for the students.
How We Work

How we work

Open

Our meetings and decisions are open to the student body. Any student may see what the Association is working on.

For everyone

We represent every student at the College, and any student may attend a meeting or raise a concern.

Practical

We turn student feedback into concrete improvements on campus.

How We're Organized

How SGA is set up

SGA has three parts.

Executive Board

The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary are elected by the student body. The Student Member of the Board is appointed. Together, the five officers run SGA and lead its meetings.

The Senate

Senators who speak for each class, plus at-large and international seats. They vote on what SGA does and recognize new clubs.

Committees

Eight committees that each handle a specific area, from advocacy to campus life, and bring their work back to the Senate.

Our History

Student leadership since 1954

The University of Virginia's College at Wise opened in 1954, and students have helped shape campus life ever since. Many of the College's traditions and organizations exist because students advocated for them.

That work continues with every new class of students, including you, should you choose to take part.

Meet this year's members

  • Elections held every year
  • Open meetings each fall and spring semester
  • A say in how the student activity budget is spent
  • Works with clubs, athletics, and campus life
Everyone Belongs Here

Inclusion

SGA represents every student at UVA Wise, and we mean every student. We do not discriminate based on age, color, disability, gender identity or expression, national or ethnic origin, political affiliation, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other part of who you are.

We also keep a calendar of national holidays and religious and cultural observances so no one gets overlooked. If you ever feel left out or unheard, come talk to us. That is exactly what we are here for.

Want to be part of it?

Come to a meeting, run for a seat, or start a club. Anyone can get involved.

Weekly Meetings

Every student is welcome

SGA meets every week during the fall and spring semesters. Any student can come, watch, and speak to the Senate during the open floor.

  • Bring a concern, idea, or proposal to the open floor
  • See how the activity fee is being spent
  • Find out what's being voted on that week
  • No sign-up needed. Just show up.

Meeting Snapshot

When: Fridays at 1 p.m.
Where: Dogwood Room, 5th Floor, Slemp Student Center
Who: All UVA Wise students. Open to the public.
Agenda: Posted ahead of each meeting

Get Involved

There are several ways to get involved with the Student Government Association, from attending a meeting to running for a seat.

Four Ways In

Ways to get involved

Run for Office

Campaign for an executive or Senate seat and represent your class directly.

Attend a Meeting

SGA meetings are open to everyone. Come by Fridays at 1 p.m. to bring up an idea or just see how it works.

Charter a Club

Start a new club and make it official through SGA.

Request Funding

Apply for financial support for your organization's events and projects.

Committees

Our committees

Each committee handles one area and works with a campus office. Every senator sits on a committee, so this is where a lot of the work happens once you're elected.

Advocacy & Opportunity

Promotes belonging and welcome for all students, planning events around diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Student Engagement

Works with the Office of Student Engagement to keep club and organization chartering efficient.

Campus Life

Looks after buildings, dorms, grounds, and dining, working with Chartwells, Residence Life, and facilities.

Academic & Student Affairs

Works with the academic dean and departments and keeps students informed of academic changes.

Events

Plans and executes campus traditions across the fall and spring, including Homecoming and Cavapalooza.

Leadership & Local Outreach

Connects SGA with campus and community leaders and serves the town of Wise through outreach.

Election & Policy

Amends and upholds the bylaws of the Student Government Association on behalf of the student body.

Enrollment

Works with Admissions and senior leadership to support the College's growth and the student experience.

Elections

Run for a seat

Each year, students elect the President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary, along with the Senate. It's more straightforward than most people expect. Here's what it takes:

  • Be a student in good academic standing
  • Pick up a candidacy packet from the SGA office
  • Collect the required signatures from other students
  • Campaign, then let students vote

Ask About Candidacy

Election Timeline

Fall: Freshman & special elections open in September.

Spring: General elections for the executive board and all Senate seats.

Anytime: Open seats can be filled by appointment. Reach out if you're interested mid-year.

Steps to Charter

  1. Gather at least the minimum number of founding members.
  2. Draft a simple constitution and mission statement.
  3. Find a faculty or staff advisor.
  4. Submit your charter application to SGA.
  5. Present to the Senate for approval.
Student Organizations

Charter a new club

Want to start a club that doesn't exist yet? SGA is how student organizations become official. Once you're chartered, you can request funding, reserve campus space, and put on events. The Student Engagement Committee and the Office of Student Engagement handle the process.

Clubs at Wise range from academic groups to service organizations to intramural teams.

Start a Charter

Allocation Requests

Request funding for your org

SGA allocates student activity funds to support events, travel, supplies, and programming that benefit the student body. If your chartered organization has a project in mind, submit an Allocation Request and we'll take it from there.

  • Open to all chartered student organizations
  • Submit the form by noon the Wednesday before the SGA meeting
  • Present your request to SGA for review
  • Receive a funding decision from the Senate

Open the Allocations Request Form ↗

Good to Know

Requests are reviewed on a rolling basis while funds remain. Submitting early gives your organization the best chance of approval.

Questions about eligibility or the process? The Treasurer and Finance Committee are happy to help you prepare.

Questions

Frequently asked

Do I have to be elected to be involved in SGA?

You don't need a seat to take part. Any student can attend meetings, volunteer at events, charter or join a club, and bring ideas to the open floor. Committee work, though, is for elected members: senators and officers staff the committees.

How much time does it take?

It depends on your role. Coming to a meeting is about an hour a week. Serving as a senator or officer, plus the committee work that comes with it, takes more. The easiest way to start is to show up to a Friday meeting.

Who can charter a club?

Any group of currently enrolled students with a shared interest, a willing advisor, and a simple constitution can apply to charter a new organization through SGA.

When are elections held?

Freshman and special elections are held in the fall, and general elections for all seats take place in the spring. Watch the events page and your student email for exact dates.

How do I bring an issue to SGA?

Come to any meeting and speak during the open floor, talk to a senator directly, or use our contact form.

Not sure where to start?

Just reach out. Tell us what you're interested in and we'll point you in the right direction.
